questions.q: What is the service recovery paradox?
questions.a: The service recovery paradox is the idea that a guest whose complaint is resolved well can end up more satisfied than one who never had a problem. Six months of POS-linked survey data from a QSR brand with 100+ locations backs it up. Guests who redeemed a recovery offer returned more often than guests who'd had a good experience.

questions.q: How do you win back an unhappy restaurant guest?
questions.a: Respond quickly with a personal acknowledgment, then send one simple recovery offer tied to a return visit. After that, follow up with guests who haven't redeemed it yet, by SMS or email a few days later. Running these three steps every time turns complaints into return visits.

questions.q: Is sending a recovery voucher enough to bring guests back?
questions.a: Sending the voucher on its own doesn't drive loyalty, because redemption is what brings the guest back. In the data, guests who received a voucher but never used it returned at lower rates than both redeemers and happy guests. A follow-up nudge is what gets more guests to actually use the offer.

questions.q: How fast should a restaurant respond to a complaint?
questions.a: Aim to respond within 24 hours. A fast, personal reply tells the guest they've been heard before any offer arrives. The time right after a complaint is when a guest decides whether to come back or leave for good.

questions.q: How can I automate guest recovery across many locations?
questions.a: You can automate it with software that triggers a recovery offer when a low rating comes in and sends follow-up nudges to guests who haven't redeemed. Momos Guest AI runs this loop automatically, so it doesn't depend on a store manager remembering to follow up. That keeps recovery consistent across every location.
